c33_pro_thinking_005.label: Using Percentiles to Tighten Forecast Intervals
c33_pro_thinking_005.description: Monte Carlo simulation provides percentiles (e.g., 10th, 50th, 90th) that allow you to say outcomes have a certain percentage chance of being below a value, narrowing a wide worst-case/best-case range to a more realistic interval like the 10th to 90th percentile.
coverage_criteria: Given a simulation output table, student can identify that the 10th and 90th percentiles define a range with about 80% confidence, and explain how it reduces uncertainty from extreme scenarios.

anchors.locator: [13:13] Examining the Results of the Simulations

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: At [13:13] the speaker interprets percentiles: '90% of simulated outcomes less than or equal to 55' and later says the realistic range is 40-41 to 54 instead of 34-61.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a key interpretive skill, testable by asking to pick the appropriate range from a simulation output.
